items.q: New headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain on chewing and ESR 90 in a 72 year old need which immediate action?
o: Start high dose steroids immediately for suspected giant cell arteritis, biopsy within about a week
items.exp: Giant cell arteritis blinds irreversibly via optic ischaemia, so steroids start on clinical suspicion while temporal biopsy (still positive for days) confirms granulomatous arteritis. Jaw claudication is the most specific symptom.
r: Incorrect. Delay risks permanent blindness.
Correct. Steroids now, biopsy promptly after.
Incorrect. This constellation is vascular until disproven.
Incorrect. Anticoagulation does not suppress arteritis.
items.kp: Jaw claudication over fifty: steroids first, questions later.

items.q: Pulseless young woman with arm claudication, bruits and unequal blood pressures suggests which large vessel vasculitis?
items.exp: Takayasu inflames aorta and branches in young (usually female) patients causing stenoses, absent pulses, pressure discrepancies and renovascular hypertension, imaged by MR or CT angiography.
r: Incorrect. Giant cell affects over fifties cranially.
Correct. Young pulseless disease means Takayasu.
Incorrect. Polyarteritis is medium vessel visceral ANCA negative.
Incorrect. Buerger thromboangiitis affects smoker limb small vessels.
items.kp: Young plus pulseless equals Takayasu until proven otherwise.

items.q: Visceral microaneurysms, mononeuritis multiplex, renovascular hypertension, hepatitis B link, ANCA negative and NO glomerulonephritis indicate what?
items.exp: Polyarteritis nodosa necrotises medium arteries forming microaneurysms and nerve infarcts while sparing glomerular capillaries (hypertension is renovascular, urine lacks nephritic sediment) and often ANCA negative, sometimes HBV driven.
r: Incorrect. Microscopic disease is MPO pauci immune glomerular.
Correct. Medium vessel aneurysms without nephritis mean PAN.
Incorrect. GPA is PR3 granulomatous upper airway disease.
Incorrect. Cryoglobulins cause small vessel purpura with low C4.
items.kp: Aneurysms plus no glomerulonephritis equals polyarteritis.

items.q: Prolonged fever, strawberry tongue, conjunctivitis, rash and coronary aneurysm risk in a 3 year old define which vasculitis needing immunoglobulin?
items.exp: Kawasaki medium vessel vasculitis of young children threatens coronary artery aneurysms, prevented by timely intravenous immunoglobulin and aspirin within the febrile window. Mucocutaneous features complete criteria.
r: Incorrect. IgA causes palpable purpura and nephritis without coronary pattern.
Correct. Febrile mucocutaneous child at coronary risk is Kawasaki.
Incorrect. Scarlet fever lacks aneurysm vasculitis course.
Incorrect. Takayasu affects older children and young adults large vessels.
items.kp: Febrile child plus coronary risk equals Kawasaki. Give IVIG early.

items.q: Asthma preceding eosinophilia, mononeuritis and pauci immune vasculitis indicates which ANCA syndrome?
items.exp: EGPA evolves through allergic asthma and eosinophilia into necrotising small vessel vasculitis with neuropathy and sometimes MPO ANCA, extravascular granulomas distinguishing it from hypereosinophilic syndrome.
r: Incorrect. GPA centres destructive upper airway granulomas PR3.
Correct. Asthma plus eosinophils plus vasculitis means EGPA.
Incorrect. Renal limited MPA lacks asthma eosinophil prodrome.
Incorrect. Goodpasture is anti GBM linear lung kidney disease.
items.kp: Asthma first, vessels later: EGPA sequence.

items.q: Saddle nose deformity, subglottic stenosis, cavitating lung nodules and PR3 ANCA indicate which vasculitis?
items.exp: GPA granulomatous inflammation destroys upper airway cartilage (saddle nose, subglottic narrowing) with lung nodules and pauci immune crescentic nephritis under PR3 cANCA. Cyclophosphamide or rituximab based induction saves organs.
r: Incorrect. EGPA is asthma eosinophil dominant.
Correct. Destructive airways plus PR3 mean GPA.
Incorrect. PAN spares airways and glomeruli aneurysming viscera.
Incorrect. Giant cell affects elderly large cranial arteries.
items.kp: Saddle nose plus PR3 equals granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

items.q: Violaceous plaques and nodules in advanced HIV from HHV8 spindle cell vessels diagnose what?
items.exp: Kaposi sarcoma is HHV8 driven vascular neoplasm of immunosuppression (skin, mouth, gut, lung) improving with antiretroviral immune recovery plus chemotherapy when visceral. Bartonella bacillary angiomatosis mimics it but needs antibiotics, distinguished by biopsy and stains.
r: Incorrect. Mimic distinguished histologically, treated by antibiotics.
Correct. HHV8 violaceous tumours mean Kaposi sarcoma.
Incorrect. Scalp angiosarcoma affects elderly HIV negative patients.
Incorrect. Cherry angiomas are tiny benign ageing lesions.
items.kp: HHV8 plus immunosuppression equals Kaposi. Check for the Bartonella mimic.

items.q: Angiosarcoma of liver classically follows exposure to which industrial carcinogens?
items.exp: Hepatic angiosarcoma is the sentinel tumour of vinyl chloride workers (also arsenic and historic Thorotrast contrast), malignant endothelium with dismal prognosis, distinct from hepatocellular carcinoma drivers.
r: Incorrect. Asbestos targets pleura and lung primarily.
Correct. Vinyl chloride causes hepatic angiosarcoma.
Incorrect. Silica fibroses lung upper lobes.
Incorrect. Benzene causes marrow aplasia and leukaemia.
items.kp: Vinyl chloride plus liver vascular cancer equals angiosarcoma.

items.q: Infantile haemangioma natural history is characteristically what?
o: Present full size at birth, never regresses
Proliferates in first months then slowly involutes over years, GLUT1 positive
items.exp: Infantile haemangiomas (GLUT1 positive endothelial tumours) appear or grow postnatally, proliferate then involute leaving fibrofatty residuum, treated by propranolol when threatening vision, airway or ulcerating. Congenital haemangiomas are fully formed at birth GLUT1 negative.
r: Incorrect. That describes congenital haemangioma behaviour.
Correct. Grow then involute: infantile haemangioma.
Incorrect. Malignant change is not expected.
Incorrect. Most need only observation or propranolol selectively.
items.kp: Strawberry mark that grows then fades: infantile haemangioma.

items.q: Thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger disease) most characteristically affects whom and how?
o: Young male heavy smokers with distal limb inflammatory thrombotic occlusion and migratory phlebitis
items.exp: Buerger disease is non atherosclerotic inflammatory thrombosis of small and medium limb vessels in young heavy tobacco users causing distal ischaemia, ulcers and migratory superficial phlebitis, treated essentially by absolute tobacco cessation.
r: Incorrect. Age and vessel pattern differ for Takayasu large disease.
Correct. Young smoker distal occlusion means Buerger disease.
Incorrect. Coronary childhood disease is Kawasaki vasculitis.
Incorrect. Diabetes accelerates atherosclerosis, not this entity.
items.kp: Young smoker losing fingers: Buerger until tobacco stops.
